objects.name: Fake imToken download sites push an Android app that sends recovery phrases and private keys to one server: technical analysis
objects.description: Copies of imToken's Chinese website offer an Android app from outside the official store. It is not imToken. NSS downloaded it and read its code: it sends the recovery phrase of every wallet created or imported in it to pt888999[.]com, and private keys to api[.]quick-node[.]com, a name that imitates QuickNode, which is not involved. On 13 November 2026 both names pointed to one server. Block both domains, look for the package com[.]anonymous[.]wallet, and treat any wallet made in it as exposed. NSS recorded 53 of the look-alike names; 40 were on no threat list NSS takes in on 13 November.

objects.name: Domain pt888999[.]com
objects.description: Receives the recovery phrase and account list of every wallet the app creates or imports (POST /api/task/batch_update); registered 3 Jul 2025; resolved to 195[.]245[.]242[.]143 on 13 Nov 2026; on no threat list NSS takes in

objects.name: Domain api[.]quick-node[.]com
objects.description: The app's main back end: receives phrase creation, wallet creation, phrase and key import, keystore export and every transfer, private key included; imitates QuickNode, a real blockchain-node provider that is not involved; a browser is sent on to the real provider's site; resolved to 195[.]245[.]242[.]143 on 13 Nov 2026; on no threat list NSS takes in

objects.name: Domain quick-node[.]com
objects.description: Registered 2025-06-20; rates High because its own DNS publishes the private-key collector; its www host copies QuickNode's site. QuickNode is not involved, and the domain is not attributed to an operator. Block this name only, never the real provider's domain
